title: Europe Battles Record Wildfires Amid Extreme Heat
subtitle: Firefighters struggle to contain massive blazes as authorities allow some residents to return home.

summary.en: Southern Europe is facing a dangerous summer as extreme heat fuels record-breaking wildfires. Thousands of people have been forced to leave their homes, and tragic losses have been reported among firefighting crews. While some evacuation orders in Spain have been lifted, the situation remains critical across the continent. Scientists warn that climate change is making these fire seasons longer and more intense. European leaders are now calling for better coordination and new resources to manage these growing threats.
summary.zh: 南歐正面臨危險的夏季，極端高溫助長了破紀錄的野火。數千人被迫離開家園，消防隊員中也傳出悲劇性的傷亡。儘管西班牙部分撤離令已解除，但整個歐洲大陸的情況依然危急。科學家警告，氣候變遷正使火災季節變得更長、更猛烈。歐洲各國領袖現正呼籲加強協調並投入新資源，以管理這些日益嚴峻的威脅。

paragraphs.en: Across southern Europe, countries are fighting a series of dangerous wildfires that have forced hundreds of thousands of people to flee their homes. From the Atlantic coast of France to the islands of Greece, firefighters are struggling against a combination of record-breaking heat and dry conditions. According to The Guardian, three firefighters have lost their lives while working to stop the flames in Greece. This ongoing crisis has alarmed experts, who note that many of these fires are burning out of control near towns and cities.
paragraphs.zh: 南歐各國正與一系列危險的野火搏鬥，迫使數十萬人逃離家園。從法國的大西洋沿岸到希臘的各個島嶼，消防人員正努力對抗破紀錄的高溫與乾燥氣候。根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，希臘已有三名消防員在救火過程中殉職。這場持續中的危機令專家感到憂心，他們指出，許多火勢已在城鎮附近失控燃燒。

paragraphs.en: In Spain, there is a small sign of progress. The government has begun to lift evacuation orders in parts of the Madrid province, allowing tens of thousands of residents to return home. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez visited a command center near the fire zone and told reporters that the situation is improving. However, he warned that the next 12 hours would be decisive for the success of the firefighting efforts. Despite this, other areas remain in danger. For instance, a fire near València remains out of control, and authorities are keeping a close watch on the weather as temperatures are expected to stay high.
paragraphs.zh: 在西班牙，情況出現了一絲進展。政府已開始解除馬德里省部分地區的撤離令，讓數萬名居民得以返家。總理桑傑士（Pedro Sánchez）視察了火場附近的指揮中心，並向記者表示情況正在好轉。然而，他警告接下來的十二小時將是救火行動能否成功的關鍵。儘管如此，其他地區仍處於危險之中。例如，瓦倫西亞附近的一場火災仍未受控，且由於氣溫預計將持續偏高，當局正密切監控天氣狀況。

paragraphs.en: France is also facing a difficult situation. According to Deutsche Welle (DW), the country is dealing with a massive blaze in the Gironde region that is four times the size of Paris. French authorities have had to move around 220,000 people to safety, including many tourists at coastal resorts. While a calm night recently allowed crews to stop some flare-ups, officials remain worried. The Meteo France weather service has issued heat warnings for most of the country, with temperatures expected to reach 40 degrees Celsius in some areas. Fire commander Matthieu Jomain stated that crews are working hard to stop any new smoke, but the hot, windy weather makes their job much harder.
paragraphs.zh: 法國也面臨嚴峻局勢。根據德國之聲（Deutsche Welle）報導，該國正處理吉倫特省一場規模達巴黎四倍大的森林大火。法國當局已不得不將約二十二萬人撤離至安全地帶，其中包括許多在濱海度假勝地的遊客。雖然近期一個平靜的夜晚讓救災人員得以遏止部分復燃，但官員們仍感到擔憂。法國氣象局已對全國大部分地區發布高溫警報，部分地區氣溫預計將達到攝氏四十度。消防指揮官喬曼（Matthieu Jomain）表示，救災人員正努力撲滅任何新冒出的濃煙，但炎熱且多風的天氣讓工作變得更加困難。

paragraphs.en: This summer has been particularly difficult for southern Europe. Data from the European Forest Fire Information System shows that wildfires have burned a record-breaking area of France. Furthermore, both France and Spain have seen a higher number of fires than usual for this time of year. For many residents, the return home has been heartbreaking. Some people, like 74-year-old José Fernández, returned to find that their homes had been completely destroyed by the fire. He told reporters that he had lost his home and all his belongings, leaving him with nothing.
paragraphs.zh: 今年夏天對南歐來說格外艱難。歐洲森林火災資訊系統的數據顯示，野火在法國燒毀的面積已創下歷史新高。此外，法國與西班牙今年此時的火災數量也高於往年。對許多居民而言，返家之路令人心碎。像七十四歲的費南德茲（José Fernández）這樣的一些民眾，回到家後發現房子已被大火完全摧毀。他告訴記者，他失去了家園與所有財產，變得一無所有。

paragraphs.en: Scientists explain that climate change is a major factor in this crisis. Hotter and drier summers are creating perfect conditions for fires to start and spread quickly. These conditions turn forests and dry land into "tinderboxes"—areas that catch fire very easily. Because of this, the fire season is lasting longer than before, and some officials worry that fires could continue to burn as late as November. The heat is also making it harder for firefighters to control the flames, as the dry vegetation burns more intensely.
paragraphs.zh: 科學家解釋，氣候變遷是這場危機的主要因素。更炎熱、更乾燥的夏季為火災的發生與迅速蔓延創造了完美條件。這些環境讓森林與乾燥土地變成了「引火物」，極易引發火勢。正因如此，火災季節比以往更長，一些官員擔心火勢可能會持續燃燒至十一月。高溫也讓消防員更難控制火勢，因為乾燥的植被燃燒得更加猛烈。

paragraphs.en: In response to these challenges, the European Union is looking for ways to improve how it handles disasters. Currently, the EU only provides extra help when a member country asks for it during an emergency. However, as fires become more extreme, there is a push for better forest management and more investment in prevention. The EU is even working on purchasing its own permanent fleet of firefighting aircraft to help member states. As one official noted, the climate is changing quickly, and the response from European nations must evolve just as fast to keep people safe.
paragraphs.zh: 為了應對這些挑戰，歐盟正尋求改善災害處理方式的方法。目前，歐盟僅在成員國於緊急情況下提出請求時提供額外援助。然而，隨著火災變得愈發極端，各界呼籲加強森林管理並增加預防工作的投資。歐盟甚至正致力於採購專屬的常備消防飛機隊，以協助成員國。正如一位官員所言，氣候正在快速變遷，歐洲各國的應對措施也必須同步快速演進，才能保障民眾安全。

paragraphs.en: For now, the focus remains on protecting lives and property. With heatwaves continuing to hit the region, the risk of new fires remains high. Firefighters from across Europe are working together, but the scale of the destruction has shown just how vulnerable the continent has become. As the summer continues, authorities are urging people to stay alert and follow safety instructions, as the battle against these extreme fires is far from over.
paragraphs.zh: 目前，重點仍放在保護生命與財產安全。隨著熱浪持續襲擊該地區，發生新火災的風險依然很高。來自歐洲各地的消防員正攜手合作，但災難的規模顯示出歐洲大陸已變得多麼脆弱。隨著夏季持續，當局呼籲民眾保持警覺並遵守安全指示，因為這場對抗極端野火的戰役遠未結束。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To officially end a rule, law, or restriction.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（電梯）或動詞（舉起），這裡指解除命令。文中：The government has begun to lift evacuation orders in parts of the Madrid province, allowing tens of thousands of residents to return home.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Sudden, brief periods where a fire becomes active or intense again.
keyTerms.noteZh: 由動詞 flare up 轉變而來的名詞，指火勢短暫復燃。文中：While a calm night recently allowed crews to stop some flare-ups, officials remain worried.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Places that are very dry and easily catch fire.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 極易著火的地方（引火物）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 原意指「火絨盒」，這裡比喻極度乾燥、極易引發火災的區域。文中：These conditions turn forests and dry land into "tinderboxes"—areas that catch fire very easily.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A strong effort to achieve something.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（推），這裡作名詞，指為了達成目標而做的努力。文中：However, as fires become more extreme, there is a push for better forest management and more investment in prevention.

quiz.question: What is the current status of the evacuation situation in Spain according to the article?

options.A: All evacuation orders across the country have been officially lifted.
options.B: Authorities have begun allowing some residents in Madrid province to go back home.
options.C: The government has ordered all tourists to leave the coastal resorts immediately.
options.D: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced that all fire risks in the country have ended.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 B。根據文章第二段，西班牙政府已開始解除馬德里省部分地區的撤離令，允許數萬名居民返家。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章提到瓦倫西亞附近仍有失控火災；選項 C 錯誤，文中提到撤離遊客的是法國而非西班牙；選項 D 錯誤，總理僅表示情況正在改善，並警告接下來 12 小時至關重要，並未宣布風險已完全解除。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, what is a likely consequence of the 'tinderbox' conditions mentioned in the text?

options.A: Firefighters will be able to extinguish fires more quickly than in previous years.
options.B: The fire season will likely become shorter as the vegetation burns up completely.
options.C: It will become increasingly difficult for authorities to contain wildfires before they spread.
options.D: The European Union will immediately stop all forest management activities to save money.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 C。文章第五段提到氣候變遷導致夏季更熱更乾，使森林變成「火藥庫」（tinderboxes），極易起火且燃燒更劇烈。結合第六段提到歐盟正尋求更好的森林管理與投資，可以推論出這些極端環境條件使得火災更難控制，迫使各國必須提升應對能力。選項 A 與文章描述的困難相悖；選項 B 錯誤，文章明確指出火災季節反而變長；選項 D 與文意相反，歐盟正在增加預防投資而非停止。

quiz.question: In the fifth paragraph, what does the word 'tinderboxes' imply about the forests?

options.A: They are being used as storage areas for emergency firefighting supplies.
options.B: They have become highly flammable and prone to catching fire easily.
options.C: They are being protected by special government-funded fire barriers.
options.D: They are areas where firefighters have successfully cleared all dry vegetation.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 B。在文中，作者用 "tinderboxes"（火藥庫/引火物盒）來形容因高溫乾燥而變得極度易燃的森林。這是一個隱喻，用來強調這些區域只要有一點火星就可能引發大火。選項 A、C、D 皆與文中描述的危險情境完全不符，這些選項誤解了該詞在描述極端火災風險時的修辭意義。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the wildfires in southern Europe?

options.A: The wildfires are primarily caused by human negligence in coastal tourist areas.
options.B: Individual countries are successfully managing the fires without needing external help.
options.C: Climate change is creating extreme conditions that require a more unified and evolved response to wildfires.
options.D: The economic impact of the fires is limited only to the destruction of private homes.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 C。文章整體論述了南歐面臨的極端火災危機，並指出氣候變遷是主因（第五段），同時強調現有的應對機制（如歐盟的援助方式）需要升級與進化（第六段），以應對未來更頻繁的災難。選項 A 過度簡化原因；選項 B 忽略了文中提到歐盟正致力於加強合作與資源共享；選項 D 錯誤，文章強調的是對生命、財產及環境的全面威脅，不僅限於經濟損失。
